newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-DOOR MAY BE OPENING FOR JOHNSON TO RACE IN ATHENS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DOOR MAY BE OPENING FOR JOHNSON TO RACE IN ATHENS.

text.p: The International Amateur Athletic Federation on Friday inched closer to a plan which would allow world champions the automatic right to defend their title.

Such a move would clear the way for Michael Johnson and other injured American track stars to compete at the world championships in August, despite the rules of their own governing body which make them ineligible to compete.

"If the U.S. federation says it would support such a move, this in certain measure opens the way for the IAAF to examine the possibility of inviting champions and world record holders to Athens," IAAF spokesman Giorgio Reineri said.
U.S. track officials said on Thursday they would welcome the IAAF inviting all 1995 world champions to defend their titles.
Speaking from the IAAF's Monaco headquarters on Friday, Reineri said: "Not just (world 400 metres champion Michael) Johnson, but other athletes could benefit (from such a rule change)."
He said world champion shot putter John Godina, who finished outside the top three at the U.S. trials, would be able to take part in Athens if the idea was introduced.

Many nations reserve places on their Olympic and world championships teams for their elite athletes, but under strict U.S. qualifying rules, only those who finish in the top three at the U.S. championships are eligible for the American team.
The world championships, only launched 14 years ago, are looking to differentiate themselves from the Olympic Games and inviting title holders could be another step.
"It's like that in skiing," Reineri said.
The suggestion arose during the current U.S. national championships which world champions Johnson, Dan O'Brien and Gwen Torrence are all missing through injury.
A decision now rests with the IAAF and, if favourable, could be introduced for Athens if it were taken inside a July 23 deadline.
